If $D$ is the finite region enclosed by the lines $x=1,$ $y=0$ and $y=2,$ and the curve $x=(y-1)^{2}+2,$ as shown above, then ${∬}_{D}xy\,dA=$
question.worked_solution:
First, let's represent $D$ as a type II region. To determine the left and right functions, we draw a horizontal arrow from left to right through the region, as usual.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14154225/assets/72cf3a4044e83e63e579b00d3ca246071787ed4d6b44e4e22fcf963dc10917b4.png)

As a result, we get

$$
D=\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le y\le 2,\,1\le x\le (y-1)^{2}+2\}.
$$

Therefore, we can express the integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}f(x,y)\,dA & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{1}^{(y-1)^{2}+2}xy\,dx\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}[{\int }_{1}^{(y-1)^{2}+2}xy\,dx]dy\end{aligned}
$$
